limitations: Uniform model neurons, assumed transmitter signs and simplified inputs limit these findings to this model. Escape and walking comparisons remain insufficient; no claim concerns what living flies require.
original: In this model, measured wiring stays stable at couplings where degree- and sign-matched shuffles saturate: the original circuit averaged 2.65 Hz at coupling 0.039, compared with null medians of 110.73 to 119.78 Hz, with Holm p 0.008 in each family.
summary: The strength-preserving comparison did not replicate the registered stability result in the 2,641-neuron circuit: N-STRENGTH had Holm p 0.088 for both metrics.

The stability difference also holds in the full 166,700-neuron MaleCNS graph, under this model and for the families that reached significance. N-SIGN reached Holm p 0.04; N-STRENGTH did not replicate (Holm p 0.14).

The stability difference also holds in the 43,894-neuron circuit, under this model and for the families that reached significance. N-FULL and N-SIGN each reached Holm p 0.02 for both metrics; N-STRENGTH did not replicate: its critical-coupling comparison was not significant (Holm p 1), and its measured rate was higher, the opposite direction (Holm p 0.02).
